editorial_contributions.text:
The authors investigate \((\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})\)--avoiding permutations. It is well known that every permutation \(\pi\) gives rise to a poset \(P_{\pi}\), where \(i\prec j\) in \(P_{\pi}\) if and only if \(i<j\) and \(i\) appears to the left of \(j\) in \(\pi\). The authors call a permutation \(\pi\) \((\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})\)-avoiding, if its poset \(P_{\pi}\) is \((\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})\)-free. This means that the poset \(P_{\pi}\) contains no induced subposet isomorphic to the disjoint union of a 3-element chain and a 1-element chain.

In this article the authors characterize completely the structure of such \((\mathbf{3}+\mathbf{1})\)-avoiding permutations. They give an exact formula for the generating function of these permutations.

editorial_contributions.text: The authors state and prove a variant of (a special case of) Turán's problem: The spectral radius of a graph is the largest eigenvalue of the graph's adjacency matrix. Then for \(k>5\) and \(n\) sufficiently large, the family of such \(W_{2k+1}\)-avoiding graphs on \(n\) vertices with spectral radius equal to \(\lambda_n\) can be characterised in a concise way.

Summary: The subject of this paper is related with some famous results of P. Erdős and E. Wirsing, concerning the characterizations of \(\log n\) or \(\log n+ O(1)\) in the class of additive arithmetic functions. 


First, we prove the stability (in the sense of Ulam-Hyers) of the additivity equation \(f(mn)- f(m)- f(n) =0\) on \(\mathbb{N}\). Finally, some other results concerning \(\delta\)-additive arithmetical functions (i.e. \(f\) satisfying \(\| f(mn)- f(m)- f(n)\|< \delta\)) are proved.

This paper is concerned with the asymptotic stability of abstract evolution equation 
\[

Applications are made to a fairly general class of strongly dissipative problems (e.g. semilinear hyperbolic second order equations, strongly damped wave type equations, the ''beam'' equation and the quasilinear wave equation with dissipation). editorial_contributions.text: Summary: We study the total number of occurrences of several vincular (also called generalized) patterns and other statistics, such as the major index and the Denert statistic, on permutations avoiding a pattern of length 3, extending results of \textit{M. The tools we use are bijections with Dyck paths, generating functions, and block decompositions of permutations.

editorial_contributions.text:
The main theorem of this paper states that for any complex hypersurface \(Z \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1}\) and a compact set \(K \subset Z\) there exists a pseudoconvex Runge domain \(U \subset Z\) containing \(K\) which has a complete proper holomorphic embedding into the unit ball \(B_{n+1} \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1}\). As an application of this theorem the authors prove that for \(n = 1\) a finite topology of \(D\) can be prescribed.

The first such results are due to \textit{P. W. Jones} [Proc. Am. Math. Soc. 76, 305--306 (1979; Zbl 0418.32006)] who construcded complete bounded holomorphic embedding of the unit disc \(B_1 \subset \mathbb{C}\) to \(\mathbb{C}^3\) and a proper complete embedding of \(B_1\) to \(B_4\). Later the first author, Forstnerič and the third author [\textit{A. Alarcón} and \textit{F. Forstnerič}, Math. Ann. 357, No. 3, 1049--1070 (2013; Zbl 1288.32014); Invent. Math. 196, No. 3, 733--771 (2014; Zbl 1297.32009); Math. Ann. 363, No. 3--4, 913--951 (2015; Zbl 1343.53053); \textit{A. Alarcón} and the third author, Math. Ann. 355, No. 2, 429--455 (2013; Zbl 1269.53061)] constructed proper complete embeddings of open and bordered Riemann surfaces to \(B_3\). \textit{B. Drinovec Drnovšek} [J. Math. Anal. Appl. 431, No. 2, 705--713 (2015; Zbl 1326.32048)] proved a similar result for bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains in high-dimensional balls.

The present paper is based on a refinement of  the approach of  the second author [Ann. Math. (2) 182, No. 3, 1067--1091 (2015; Zbl 1333.32018)], used to find an embedded complete closed complex hypersurface in \(B_{n+1}\).

The proof of the main theorem is divided into several steps. First the obstacles \(\{T_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{N}_0}\) in \(B_{n+1} \setminus \frac{1}{2}\overline{B}_{n+1}\) are created. The (disjoint) sets \(T_j\), \(j \in \mathbb{N}\), are (real) (\(2n+1\))-dimensional balls tangent to spheres \(\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}(0,r_j)\), \(r_j < 1\), and they are positioned in such a way that any closed hypersurface in \(B_{n+1}\) avoiding them winds so wildly that it is complete. Next an exhaustion \(\{E_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{N}} \) of \(B_{n+1}\) by smoothly bounded strictly pseudoconvex domains is chosen such that \(T_i \subset E_j\), \(i \leq j-1\) and \(\overline{E_j} \cap E_i = \emptyset\), \(i \geq j\). Inductively a sequence of automorphisms \(\{\Phi_j\}_{j \in \mathbb{N}}\) is constructed such that \(\Phi_j\) approximates the identity on \(E_j\), \(\Phi_j \circ \dots \circ \Phi_1(Z)\) avoids \(T_0,\ldots, T_j\) and converges on a Runge domain \(\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^{n+1} \) to a map which maps \(\Omega\) biholomorphically to the unit ball \(B_{n+1}\). The domain \(D\) is then a connected component of \(\Omega \cap Z\) containing \(K\).

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: The Delsarte extremal problem for positive definite functions, originally introduced by Delsarte in coding theory to bound the size of error-correcting codes, has since found applications in diverse areas such as sphere packing, Fuglede's spectral set conjecture, and $1$-avoiding sets. Recent developments have established the existence of extremizers in fairly general settings and identified precise linear programming dual formulations, together with strong duality results, in several important cases including finite groups and $\mathbb{R}^d$. In this paper, we consider a generalized Delsarte problem on locally compact Abelian groups, providing a natural framework for harmonic analysis. We extend both the normalization and the objective functional to encompass a wide range of previously studied cases, while avoiding restrictive topological assumptions common in the literature. Within this general setting, we derive the corresponding dual problem and prove a strong duality theorem, thereby unifying and extending earlier results. Naturally, our proof uses harmonic analysis, but the key is a functional analytic approach which distinguishes our proof from existing methods.

editorial_contributions.text:
The present paper investigates the estimation problem in models of the instantaneous short interest rate from a new perspective. The starting point is the stochastic differential equation for the instantaneous short interest rate used by K. Chan, A. Karolyi, F. Longstaff and A. Sanders (1992) (hereafter abbreviated and referred as CKLS-1992). Applying Ito's Lemma, the authors derive from CKLS-1992 the stochastic differential equation for discretely compound interest rates that are observed on financial markets. The result is a set of two stochastic differential equations, one for the unobserved instantaneous spot rate, and the other for the observed discretely compound rate. For a partially observed system, the paper proposes a filtering methodology based on a dynamic Bayesian algorithm, as a method to estimate the short rate as well as the parameters of the model from observations of discretely compound rates.


This articie is organized as follows: Section 2 presents the derivation of the stochastic dynamic system, followed by the instantaneous spot rate and discretely compound rates. The model is set up such that the short rates to take positive values to belong to a compact interval. 


Section 3 outlines the discretization technique for the continuous time stochastic differential equation system, provided that the discretised system to generate only positive interest rates with the same support as the continua time counterpart. This section contains also the dynamic Bayesian algorithm for the calculation of the spot rate distribution and of the parameters, depending on the observations. Section 4 describes the procedure used to approximate by quantization (spatial discretization) the dynamic Bayesian algorithm, such that the computations are reduced to a sequence of recursive matrix operations. The convergence of the approximations is demonstrated. Section 5 discusses the implementation of the approximating version of the dynamic Bayesian algorithm on simulated data based on some parameter values obtained in earlier empirical studies. Using conditional posterior distributions, it is proved that the resulted estimates are quite satisfactory.


The proposed methology shows several advantages: (1) avoiding the use of proxy variables; (2) the use of the updated posterior distribution to calculate a range of statistical quantities of interest; (3) the utilization of a number of available discretely compounded rates as the observed quantities; (4) design of a one-factor model of the instantaneous spot rate, model that is consistent with a set of discretely compounded rates whose maturities are relevant to the application at hand.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: We have studied the update operator \(\bigoplus_{1}\) defined for update sequences by Eiter et al. without tautologies and we have observed that it satisfies an interesting property. This property, which we call weak independence of syntax, is similar to one of the postulates proposed by Alchourrón, Gärdenfors, and Makinson (AGM); only that in this case it applies to nonmonotonic logic. In addition, we consider five other additional basic properties about update programs and we show that \(\bigoplus_{1}\) satisfies them. This work continues the analysis of the AGM postulates with respect to the \(\bigoplus_{1}\) operator under a refined view that considers \(N_{2}\) as a monotonic logic which allows us to expand our understanding of answer sets. Moreover, \(N_{2}\) helped us to derive an alternative definition of \(\bigoplus_{1}\) avoiding the use of unnecessary extra atoms.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A classical extremal problem on progression free sets is to determine the maximum size of a $3$-term arithmetic progression free set in algebraic structures, for instance in intervals of integers or in finite vector spaces. To determine the minimum size of a complete $3$-term arithmetic progression free set is a lower-end analogue of this problem. It is also closely related to complete caps and saturating sets in finite geometry. A simple counting argument shows that the order of magnitude of the minimum size is at least the square root of the cardinality of the structure. Addressing two open problems, we show that this lower bound is essentially tight. First, for every cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_m$, we give explicit constructions of complete $3$-AP-free sets whose size is less than $2\sqrt m$. For $m\ge81$ the constructed sets satisfy the stronger, so-called complete $(2,-1)$-avoiding property; the remaining cases $m<81$ are covered by a finite verification. Second, we resolve the vector space variant in a weaker sense by showing that for every fixed odd prime $p$ and $\varepsilon>0$, there is a constant $C_{p, \varepsilon}$ such that \[ a(3\text{-}\mathrm{AP},\mathbb{F}_p^n)\le C_{p, \varepsilon}\,n^{1+\varepsilon}\,p^{n/2} =p^{n/2+o(n)} \] holds for the minimum size $a(3\text{-}\mathrm{AP},\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ of a complete 3-AP-free subset of $\mathbb{F}_p^n$, for all $n\ge1$.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: Recently, \textit{T. Dokos} et al. In this paper, we confirm this conjecture for all \(k\geqslant 1\) and \(m=1\). In fact, we construct a descent set preserving bijection between \( 12\ldots k (k-1) \)-avoiding permutations and \(23\ldots k1\)-avoiding permutations for all \(k\geqslant 3\). As a corollary, our bijection enables us to settle a conjecture of \textit{N. Gowravaram} and \textit{R. Jagadeesan} [ibid. 20, No. 4, Research Paper P17, 28 p. (2013; Zbl 1300.05319)] concerning the Wilf-equivalence for permutations with given descent sets.

editorial_contributions.text: Summary: As a variation of De Bruijn graphs on strings of symbols, the graph of overlapping permutations has a directed edge \(\pi(1)\pi(2)\ldots \pi(n+1)\) from the standardization of \(\pi(1)\pi(2)\ldots \pi(n)\) to the standardization of \(\pi(2)\pi(3)\ldots \pi(n+1)\). In this paper, we consider the enumeration of \(d\)-cycles in the subgraph of overlapping \((231, 4\bar{1}32)\)-avoiding permutations. To this end, we introduce the notions of marked Motzkin paths and marked Riordan paths, where a marked Motzkin (resp. Riordan) path is a Motzkin (resp. Riordan) path in which exactly one step before the leftmost return point is marked. We show that the number of closed walks of length \(d\) in the subgraph of overlapping \((231, 4\bar{1}32)\)-avoiding permutations are closely related to the number of marked Motzkin paths and that of marked Riordan paths. ~By establishing bijections, we get the enumerations of marked Motzkin paths and marked Riordan paths. As a corollary, we provide bijective proofs of two identities involving Catalan numbers in answer to the problem posed by \textit{R. Ehrenborg} et al. [J. Comb. Theory, Ser. A 129, 1--18 (2015; Zbl 1302.05081)]. Moreover, we get the enumerations of \((231, 4\bar{1}32)\)-avoiding affine permutations and \((312, 32\bar{4}1)\)-avoiding affine permutations.

editorial_contributions.text:
A noncommutative version of the minimal supersymmetric standard model (MSSM) is presented (Chapter 4. \S4.2, (4.11)). From this model, we obtain the exact particle content of MSSM and identify its interactions. But their coefficients are such that the standard action functional used in noncommuttive geometry (cf. Chapter 1. \S 1.2.2) is not supersymmetric.

The authors say the standard model (SM) is an extremely successful theory. However, the gravitational theory is not included, there are large quadratic correction to the Higgs mass and it does not account for dark matter. Therefore, we need new theory. A candidate of new theory is the supersymmetry. In Chapter 1, after explaining supersymmetry, the MSSM is described (\S1.1.1. Example 1.4).

The MSSM is the (\(N=2\)) supersymmetric theory obtained by adding to the particle content a superpartner for each type of SM particles. In addition, to cancel a chiral anomaly, an extra Higgs doublet and its super partner are introduced with hypercharge opposite to that of the other part (cf. [\textit{M. Drees}, \textit{R. Godbole} and \textit{P. Roy}, Theory and phenomenology of sparticles. Singapore: World Scientific (2004)]. Still now, there are no experimental support of the MSSM. But it has many merits, such as 
{\parindent=6mm \begin{itemize} \item[-] For each of the loop-interaction contributing to the mass of the Higgs, there is a second such interaction that features a superpartner. This second contribution compensates for the first one. \item [-] If the \(R\)-parity; 
\[
R_p=(-1)^{2S+3B+L},
\]
 \(S\) is the spin of the particle, \(B\) is the baryon number and \(L\) is the lepton number, is conserved, the lightest particle that has \(R_p=-1\) cannot decay and this provide a cold Dark Matter candidate. \item [-] The additional particle content of the MSSM makes it possible for the three coupling constants \(g_1\), \(g_2\) and \(g_3\) to evolve via the renormalization group equations in such a way that they exactly meet at one energy scale. This hints at the existence of a grand unification theory. 

\end{itemize}} 
The rest of Chapter 1 is devoted to the review of noncommutative geometry. Besides the canonical spectral triple \((C^\infty(M), L^2(S), \partial\!\!\!/)\), \(M\) a compact spin manifold and \(S\) is the spin bundle, the finite spectral triple \((\mathcal{A}_F, \mathcal{H}_F, D_F)\), \(\mathcal{A}_F\) is a finite dimensional algebra, \(\mathcal{H}_F\) is a finite dimensional left \(\mathcal{A}_F\)-module and \(D_F:\mathcal{H}_F\to\mathcal{H}_F\) is a Hermitian matrix, is important to construct noncommutative version of the SM and MSSM. The real even spectral triple 
\[
(C^\infty(M, \mathcal{A}_F, L^2(S\otimes\mathcal{H}_F. \partial\!\!\!/+\gamma^5\otimes D_F, J_M\otimes J_F, \gamma^5\otimes\gamma_F)
\]
 is called an almost commutative geometry [\textit{B. Iochum} et al., J. Math. Phys. 45, No. 12, 5003--5041 (2004; Zbl 1064.58024)]. Note, that in the canonical spectral triple, \(C^\infty(M)\) is a commutative algebra, so it can be said commutative.

A noncommutative version of the SM is given as an almost commutative geometry (\S 1.2.3 Calculation of Higgs boson mass by using this model and some other discussions on physical significances are also given in this section). Chapter 1 is concluded to give detailed study on finite spectral triples via Krajewski diagrams (cf. [\textit{T. Krajewski}, J. Geom. Phys. 28, No. 1--2, 1--30 (1998; Zbl 0932.58006)]). This diagram is heavily used in the later discussions.

To impose \(N=2\) supersymmetry to real even spectral triple, assume it is dressed a grading \(R\); \(R:\mathcal{H}\to \mathcal{H}\) satisfies 
\[
[R,\gamma]=[R,J]=[R,a]=0, \;a\in\mathcal{A}.
\]
 Let \(M\) be a 4-dimensional flat manifold, KO-dimension of the almost commutative geometry is 2, and \(\mathcal{A}_F=\oplus_i^KM_{N_i}(\mathbb{C})\). Then in Chapter 2, dividing five cases of the building blocks (listed as Table 2.2), obstructions to impose supersymmetry to the geometry are calculated in Chapter 2. For example, it is shown if \(\mathcal{A}_F\) is consisted by three components, and whose finite Hilbert space features building blocks \(\mathcal{B}^\pm_{ij}\) and \(\mathcal{B}^\pm_{ik}\), then the action derived from the spectral action by using heat kernel expansion (given as (1.24)) is not supersymmetric (Proposition 2.19). Of course, supersymmetric cases are also given (e.g., Theorem 2.5). They take most part of the book.

In Chapter 3, soft supersymmetry breaking; breaking supersymmetry by means of a supersymmetry breaking Lagrangian (The Girardello Lagrangian treated in Chapter 3 is a little modified the Lagrangian used in this paper), is discussed and show ``all possible terms that break supersymmetry softly and that can originate from the spectral action (1.24) of an almost-commutative geometry consisting of building blocks are mass terms for scalar fields and gauginos and trilinear and bilinear couplings'' (Theorem 3.1).

The results of Chapter 2 and 3 give obstructions to construct a noncommutative MSSM, which are summarized in Chapter 4, \S4.1. Avoiding these obstructions, a noncommutative version of MSSM is presented in \S4.2 (4.11). Then, identification of particles and sparticles of this model and those of MSSM is done in \S4.3. It is noted some results obtained from this model and from SM are different. For example, relation between three coupling constants \(g_1,g_2\) and \(g_3\) in this model is 
\[
g_3^2=g_2^2=\frac{11}{9}g_1^2, 
\]
 which differs \(g_3^2=g_2^2=\dfrac{5}{3}g_1^2\) obtained from the SM (\S4.3.2). Moreover, the number of generation of this model is shown to be equal to \(\frac{1}{2}\) via analyzing the Lagrangian given from the action functional (Chapter 1. (1.21). It reflects generating inner fluctuations of the components of Dirac operators of an almost-commutative geometry). These results are summarized as

Theorem 4.1. There is no number of particle of generations for which the action (1.21) associated to the almost-commutative geometry determined by (4.11), which corresponds to the particle-content and the superpotential of the MSSM, is supersymmetric.

This is the final result of this book.
